turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Let's not waste each other's time.
Then answer me. Who decided?
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.

Not a gray area. It's a machine's guess, Hale, and the guide I have printed in my bag says it "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student." What do you have that isn't software?
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
I'm here as his mother. Is the score all you have?
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.
I'm writing that down. It isn't mine to explain, and so far it's numbers you've said aloud. Put the document in front of me.
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.
"A chatbot did." On what basis? A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare loses marks for it, and I still don't have a single page in front of me.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Save it. Then the score settles nothing by itself. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
That isn't an answer. Yes or no.
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
I'm not drafting your policy, Hale. You already have one, and it says you speak to the student first. I'm taking your silence on that as a no.
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.
No. Ten minutes. Is anything on Owen's record right now?
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
Rhythm. That's an impression, not a document. His record, Hale.
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
I'm sorry? Then end it, or answer me. Owen's record.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?

A student who changes his argument between the outline and the essay has done what an outline is for. Is that October 15 outline in this room, with the date on it? And you've now stepped past his record twice.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.
That's 4.4, and the part about his record I'll want in an email. But "once" is pressure, not evidence. A rewrite for what, when nothing has been put in front of me?
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.
Then walk. The zero is still in the gradebook, and I'll be in the principal's office before you reach your car.
